_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never shipped to the student's browser until a teacher/marker PDF is generated. English-only. Keep activityId/version in sync with config.json.

markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least two of their own Investigation Record entries as evidence (for example a Photo Lab label such as 'Cell wall' on the Elodea photo, a Build-a-Cell result for the leaf or root cell, or an Energy Lab order with its mitochondria/chloroplast numbers).
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine entries from the student's own record; exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim such as 'plant cells have extra parts' with no logged entry quoted.

markingScheme.criterion: Names at least two of the three plant-only parts (cell wall, chloroplasts, permanent vacuole) and makes clear that animal cells do not have them.
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming the nucleus, mitochondria or membrane, which animal cells also have.

markingScheme.criterion: Gives the correct function of at least two of the plant-only parts named: cell wall = protects the cell / keeps its shape / support; chloroplasts = contain chlorophyll and absorb light for photosynthesis (making food); vacuole = holds cell sap / keeps the cell firm.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct functional wording, e.g. 'the wall holds the cell in shape', 'chloroplasts make food from light'.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'The wall is for the plant' or 'chloroplasts are green' with no function stated.

markingScheme.criterion: States that mitochondria release energy for the cell by (aerobic) respiration.
markingScheme.accept: 'Mitochondria are where respiration happens', 'they make energy', 'release energy from glucose'.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'Mitochondria are the powerhouse' with no link to energy being released is borderline; award only if energy release/respiration is stated.

markingScheme.criterion: Links the muscle cell's high energy demand (contracting a lot, running) to it having many more mitochondria than a skin cell.
markingScheme.accept: 'Muscles need lots of energy so they have lots of mitochondria'.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'Muscle cells are bigger' with no reference to energy demand.

markingScheme.criterion: Decides that the student is wrong and explains that root cells are underground where there is no light, so they cannot photosynthesise and have no (or very few) chloroplasts.
markingScheme.accept: 'No light underground so no photosynthesis'; 'roots get sugar from the leaves'.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying the student is wrong with no reason, or agreeing with the student.

levels.descriptor: None of the three analytic points met: no logged entries quoted, no plant-only parts correctly named, no function given.
One of the three analytic points met: quotes two real entries, OR names at least two plant-only parts, OR gives the function of two named parts.
Two of the three analytic points met, e.g. quotes real entries and names the plant-only parts but gives no function for them.

All three analytic points present: quotes at least two of their own entries, names at least two plant-only parts (cell wall, chloroplasts, permanent vacuole) and states the correct function of at least two.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: None of the three analytic points met: mitochondria's role is not stated, the energy link is missing, and the root cell is not correctly judged.

One of the three analytic points met: states that mitochondria release energy, OR links high energy demand to many mitochondria, OR correctly rejects chloroplasts in root cells with the no-light reason.
Two of the three analytic points met, e.g. the mitochondria explanation is complete but the root-cell judgement is missing or unsupported.

All three analytic points present: mitochondria release energy by respiration, muscle's high energy demand explains the many mitochondria, and root cells have no chloroplasts because there is no light underground.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across both the Explain and Apply answers together, independent of and never overlapping with the content marks above.

levels.descriptor: Too unclear or incomplete for the reasoning to be followed; no correct scientific vocabulary.

Main meaning understandable, but organisation or precision is weak, or key terms (organelle, nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplast, cell wall, vacuole) are missing or misused. Do not deduct for minor spelling/grammar slips that do not harm meaning.
Clear, logically organised full sentences using correct scientific vocabulary, precise enough to follow easily. Minor spelling/grammar slips that do not affect meaning are not penalised.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply), using each question's point-by-point marking_scheme (award each point independently unless it states a dependsOn, in which case only award it if the point it depends on was also awarded) and the rubric level descriptors, which restate the same points as bands - do not invent extra criteria. The Explain marks ARE the use_of_evidence criterion and the Apply marks ARE the reasoning criterion (one-to-one); never award them twice. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy. Communication is judged holistically across both answers and never overlaps the content marks. The Knowledge Check was adaptive (L1-L5): every level is marked out of 100% with no cap, so do not adjust marks for the student's level. Accept scientifically valid alternative wording per each point's 'accept'; do not penalise spelling or grammar unless it makes the meaning unclear. Use the raw Investigation Record data (not just the student's summary) to verify any claim about their own entries (Photo Lab labels, Build-a-Cell wrong tries, Energy Lab mitochondria, chloroplasts, light, energy and sugar numbers). Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
